title: Intel Tech Support Ad (Intel Parody)
description: After realizing that some of their customers might be confused, Intel decided to make a new company. Intel Tech Support.

asr.full_text: Ever since Intel has been developing a new technology we feel our customers have the very much confusion. We feel that it is a very good idea to launch our new plan, Intel tech support. Intel tech support is all about helping people, if you have a question, comment or concern about whatever Intel's doing, feel free to call us! User satisfaction is guaranteed!, I am Vikram Bandi, Jr I am the head of customer service. If you would like to visit us at our stores. Here are our times Sunday, we're open at 2.37 to 2.49 p.m. Monday from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m Tuesday to Saturday, we are closed. If this is not convenient for you. I need Intel Tech Support. You are pretty much screwed but we do have a call center. I need to call Intel Tech Support. Hello? Hello, Yes, who is this? Oh yeah I'm Bob, I was wondering, I have a problem with my software. Why can't you not see, I'm pretty much busy! busy still not convinced here are some reviews of our satisfied customers ever since I called Intel tech support I keep on getting prank calls by these random starts 67 numbers and like hello do you want your Samosas oh hello Shallu kaan is in your neighborhood and come out naked naked he will come to you Man I hate Intel Tech support whenever I call him there is this Indian dude who is always putting me on hold and he never answers anything Intel Tech Support serving you ever since yesterday pa-dum-bum oh crap that's copyrighted

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an Intel parody featuring actors portraying a fictional tech-support service. The scripted customer-service dialogue and references to prank calls establish a comedic skit context, with no request for payment or private credentials described.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary context is entertainment: the title identifies a parody, the dialogue is presented as a scripted support advertisement, and the purported customer experience centers on comedic prank calls.

evidence.observation: The title explicitly identifies the video as an Intel parody and an advertisement-style presentation.
The scripted dialogue presents a fictional tech-support service and invites viewers to call.
evidence.quote: Intel tech support is all about helping people, if you have a question, comment or concern about whatever Intel's doing, feel free to call us!

evidence.observation: A purported customer review describes prank calls after contacting the fictional support service, supporting a comedic skit context.

evidence.observation: The closing line continues the mock customer-service advertisement framing.
